svg.title: Layers of provider lock-in and how to keep each movable
svg.desc: Five layers of coupling to a model provider, from easiest to hardest to move. First, the model ID: one configuration value; keep IDs in configuration and check the lifecycle fields of the models endpoints. Second, the SDK and API shape: wrap calls in an internal adapter; OpenAI-compatible endpoints help only partly. Third, prompts tuned to one model: keep prompts in your repository and an evaluation set you can rerun on any candidate. Fourth, provider-only features such as caching modes, batch jobs, background mode, stored conversations and hosted prompts: wrap them and plan for retirement, as with OpenAI's reusable prompt objects, which shut down on November 30, 2026. Fifth, data and contract terms: retention, a BAA, region and the data processing agreement must be in place before you depend on a provider and reviewed when they change. An arrow on the left points down toward harder to move.

g.text: What couples you to a provider
How to keep it movable
harder to move
Model ID
one configuration value
Keep IDs in configuration; check the models endpoints'
lifecycle fields (shutdown_date, lifecycle, retires_at).
SDK and API shape
request formats, events, errors, usage fields
Wrap calls in an internal adapter interface; OpenAI-
compatible endpoints only remove part of this layer.
Prompts tuned to one model
wording, examples, output quirks
Keep prompts in your repository and an evaluation set
that reruns on any candidate model in minutes.
Provider-only features
caching modes, batch, background, stored state
Wrap them and plan for retirement: OpenAI's reusable
prompt objects shut down on November 30, 2026.
Data and contract terms
retention, BAA, region, processing agreement
Sign them before you depend on a provider, and review
them when the provider's data pages change.
The model ID is the easy part; prompts, provider features and contracts are what actually tie you down.
